stem: The receipts in Captain ___ bundle, Mr. Quill found, showed larger payments than those in the ledger copy that the wharf had filed with the insurers in September.

rule: Captain Dunmore is one person who owns the bundle, so add an apostrophe and s: Dunmore’s. Dunmores is a plain plural, Dunmores’ would mean several Dunmores, and Dunmore shows no ownership.

stem: Weeks before the fire, Nora had taken Mr. ___ loft key from his housekeeper’s drawer, hoping to blame him, and on Thursday she bought two beeswax candles.

rule: Mr. Hallam is one man who owns the key, so add an apostrophe and s: Hallam’s. Hallams is a plain plural, Hallams’ would mean several Hallams, and Hallam shows no ownership.

stem: The lamps in the chapel hall, I learned from ___ caretaker, had been electric since the spring, and no candles had been ordered all year.
fixed: The lamps in the chapel hall, I learned from its caretaker, had been electric since the spring, and no candles had been ordered all year.
rule: Its (no apostrophe) shows ownership: the hall’s caretaker. It’s means it is or it has, and its’ and it are not correct here.

stem: Mr. Hallam said that ___ had been no cupboard in the loft since he tore the old one out three years earlier.
fixed: Mr. Hallam said that there had been no cupboard in the loft since he tore the old one out three years earlier.
rule: There begins a statement that something exists or existed. Their and theirs show ownership, and they’re means they are.

stem: Nora Tallis, with ___ hands shaking, confessed that she had planned the fire for months and signed her statement at dawn.
fixed: Nora Tallis, with her hands shaking, confessed that she had planned the fire for months and signed her statement at dawn.
rule: A pronoun must agree with its antecedent. Nora Tallis is one woman, so the pronoun is her. Their is plural, his is masculine, and its is for things.

stem: Either the clerk who wrote the receipts or the owner who signed the ledger every month had pocketed the missing money___ the audit was due on Monday.
fixed: Either the clerk who wrote the receipts or the owner who signed the ledger every month had pocketed the missing money, and the audit was due on Monday.
rule: Two complete thoughts joined by and need a comma before the and. No punctuation makes a run-on, and a semicolon or colon does not go with and.

stem: The difference between the ledger and the receipts, Mr. Quill calculated___ came to nearly four hundred pounds over two years.

stem: At about a quarter past eleven___ the flame reached the rags, and the dry boards of the loft floor, which sat above the oil store, caught at once.

rule: Put a comma after an introductory phrase. A semicolon needs a complete thought before it, a colon does not fit, and no punctuation runs the phrase into the sentence.

stem: Mr. Hallam swore that he had trusted Miss Tallis completely, had never read the figures he signed, and ___ his loft key since October.
fixed: Mr. Hallam swore that he had trusted Miss Tallis completely, had never read the figures he signed, and had not seen his loft key since October.
rule: Items in a list must be parallel. The list uses had trusted and had never read, so the last verb is had not seen. The other choices change the verb form, and did not see cannot go with since October.

stem: The buyer, according to Mr. Larkin, was a young woman with ink-stained fingers ___ said the candles were for the chapel.

rule: Use who for a person who does the action. Here she is the subject of said, so who is correct. Whom is for objects, whose shows ownership, and which is for things.

rule: The story is told in the past tense, and chained, walked, and watched are all past. So the last verb must be rang. The other choices shift to the present or future.

text: The sums in the ledger, which Nora Tallis wrote herself, was smaller then the sums the captains paid at her window, and for two years she kept the difference.
